title: Who holds each permission, on an EnumMap

blocks.text: An `EnumMap` is an array indexed by ordinal: no hashing, O(1) access, and iteration in declaration order. The page's real-world example keeps an access log keyed by permission, with an entry put in for **every** permission up front.

Write `static Map<Permission, List<String>> whoHas(Map<String, Set<Permission>> grants)` for the nested `Permission { READ, WRITE, EXECUTE, DELETE, ADMIN }`. `grants` maps each user name to the permissions that user holds. The result maps each permission to the users holding it:

items: every permission has an entry, with an empty list when nobody holds it;
the permissions iterate in declaration order;
each list of users is sorted by name.

rows: `{READ=[alice, bob, carol], WRITE=[alice], EXECUTE=[], DELETE=[], ADMIN=[carol]}`

cases.says: whoHas() maps each permission to the users that hold it.
A permission no user holds still has an entry, with its own empty list.
The map iterates permissions in declaration order (READ, WRITE, EXECUTE, DELETE, ADMIN), not alphabetically.
Each permission's users are sorted by name, whatever order the grants came in.
